meta.description: Tests which taxa differ between groups on an amplicon ASV table using compositionally-aware methods (ALDEx2, ANCOM-BC2, LinDA, MaAsLin2/3, ZicoSeq, LEfSe), delivering a consensus of >=2 tools rather than one tool's hit list, with prevalence filtering, effect-size/FDR gating, and covariate/repeated-measures handling.

scientific_integrity.detail: References unchanged from the original audit and still verified real/well-known (Fernandes 2014, Gloor 2016, Lin & Peddada 2020/2024, Mallick 2021, Nickols 2026, Zhou 2022, Yang & Chen 2022/2023, Pelto 2025, Nearing 2022, Segata 2011, Love 2014, Benjamini & Hochberg 1995). No fabricated statistics anywhere in the fixed SKILL.md.

practice_boundaries.detail: Still community/taxon-level statistics for research use; no diagnostic or prescriptive claims about individuals.

methodological_ground.detail: Failure Modes table still actively prevents fallacies (cherry-picking, pseudo-replication) and now documents two more real traps (LinDA coercion, ZicoSeq zero-variance) rather than committing them.

code_usability.detail: All 7 R code blocks now present (ALDEx2, ANCOM-BC2, LinDA, MaAsLin2, MaAsLin3, ZicoSeq, DESeq2-caveat) were independently re-executed end to end against the real fixture and completed without an R-level halt; LEfSe's CLI syntax was independently verified against real --help output. One new, real defect was found and is recorded as a P1 (see recommendations), not a veto trigger: MaAsLin2's own shown random_effects='SubjectID' code silently returns zero usable result rows on the cross-sectional fixture (an lme4 'number of levels ... must be < number of observations' error caught per-feature, not an R-level crash) -- syntactically valid, dependency-complete, and it runs to completion, so it does not meet M4's 'unrunnable' bar, but it is functionally useless for the exact repeated-measures scenario the Skill recommends it for.

functional_suitability.note: Completeness much improved: 7 of 8 named tools now have a runnable code block (only LEfSe remains CLI-only, execution-blocked by an external env, not undocumented). Correctness: both prior P1s (LinDA coercion crash, ZicoSeq zero-variance crash) are genuinely fixed and re-verified by direct execution, including a standalone re-test of the ZicoSeq fix on the RAW unfiltered fixture (not just riding along on the prv_cut filter). Docked 2 points for a newly found correctness defect: MaAsLin2's own shown random_effects='SubjectID' block silently returns zero usable rows on the fixture used throughout the rest of the Skill (independently discovered this pass, not part of the fix's scope).

reliability.note: Common Errors table now correctly documents both fixed traps (LinDA sample_data coercion, ZicoSeq zero-variance) with the exact error text and fix, verified accurate against real error messages this pass. Docked 2 points (down from a possible full score) because the newly found MaAsLin2 SubjectID/cross-sectional trap -- the same defect class -- is undocumented in this same table.

performance_context.note: Unchanged: SKILL.md length and workflow structure are unaffected by the fix; the new Installation section is short and appropriately placed.

agent_usability.note: Learnability improved: only LEfSe now requires external API inference (ZicoSeq/MaAsLin3/DESeq2 all gained real code blocks this pass). Consistency and feedback design remain strong and unchanged. Error-prevention is stronger (2 more documented failure modes verified this pass), offset by the one newly found undocumented MaAsLin2 trap.

human_usability.note: Unchanged from the original audit: still jargon-dense relative to a bench biologist's phrasing, softened by usage-guide.md's Quick Start; forgiveness is still deliberately rigid about integer-count input (a data-integrity guarantee, Category-3 override applies, not a defect).

security.note: Unchanged: no credentials/secrets, no sensitive-data retention; input validation still delegated to the underlying R packages.

maintainability.note: Improved by the redundancy pass: install notes now live once, in SKILL.md's new Installation section; usage-guide.md's 'What the Agent Will Do' and 'Tips' sections (previously fully restated from SKILL.md's own tables) were replaced with a one-line pointer, confirmed by direct inspection of the current usage-guide.md -- a real single-source-of-truth improvement. Testability remains modest: still only one bundled worked-example script, no bundled ground-truth file.

agent_specific.note: The one prior deduction (ALDEx2 missing set.seed) is fixed and independently re-verified this pass: two aldex() runs with the same seed=42 produced an identical hit set AND a bit-identical effect column. Trigger precision, composability, and escape hatches remain excellent and unchanged from the original audit.

inputs.label: MaAsLin2 with random_effects='SubjectID' on the cross-sectional fixture -- a re-auditor-discovered defect, same class as the fixed LinDA bug but in an untouched code block
inputs.note: executed: true. run/reaudit02_maaslin2_diagnostic.R and run/reaudit03_maaslin2_noplots.R. SKILL.md's own MaAsLin2 code block (unchanged by this fix pass, present verbatim since before the fix) shows fixed_effects=c('Group','Age'), random_effects=c('SubjectID') -- run verbatim against phyloseq_object.rds (40 samples, 40 unique SubjectID -- 1 sample per subject, the SAME cross-sectional fixture the fixed LinDA example now correctly avoids pairing with a subject random effect). Every one of the 192 per-feature lme4 fits fails with 'number of levels of each grouping factor must be < number of observations (problems: SubjectID)', caught internally by MaAsLin2 with a per-feature WARNING (not an R-level halt) and 'returning NA'. The written all_results.tsv ends up with ZERO rows for the Group coefficient -- a completely empty, useless result, reached without any top-level error. Confirmed this is the SubjectID/cross-sectional mismatch specifically (not a general MaAsLin2 problem) by re-running with random_effects omitted: 188 Group rows, 50 significant, TP=17/17, FP=33 -- the tool works correctly once the same cross-sectional/random-effect mismatch that was fixed for LinDA is avoided. Separately (not scored here, noted for the record): a plain Maaslin2() call that DOES have real significant results to plot crashes on plot generation with a ggplot2 API-version error ('<ggplot2::labels> object is invalid: every label must be named'), most likely an environment ggplot2-version mismatch (TOOLS.md records ggplot2 4.0.3 in this env) rather than a SKILL.md code defect -- reproducible with plot_heatmap/plot_scatter left at their defaults.

recommendations.title: MaAsLin2's own shown random_effects='SubjectID' code block silently returns zero usable rows on a cross-sectional fixture -- the same defect class already fixed for LinDA, left undocumented in the code block two sections above
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md's MaAsLin2 code block (unchanged by this fix pass) shows random_effects = c('SubjectID') as the canonical pattern for longitudinal/repeated designs. Run verbatim against the fixture used throughout the rest of the Skill's examples (40 samples, 40 unique SubjectID -- one sample per subject), every per-feature lme4 fit fails with 'number of levels of each grouping factor must be < number of observations', caught internally with only a per-feature WARNING, and the written result table ends up with zero rows for the Group coefficient -- a silently empty, useless result reached without any top-level R error.
recommendations.root_cause: A random effect grouping variable with as many levels as observations is degenerate (no within-group replication to estimate a variance component from) -- the identical mismatch class that produced the original LinDA P1 (formula '~ Group + Age + (1 | SubjectID)' against a cross-sectional fixture), but MaAsLin2's block sits in the very next section and was not touched by this fix pass because it was not part of the original audit's tested inputs.
recommendations.fix: Either change the MaAsLin2 code block's demo formula to drop random_effects (matching how the LinDA block was fixed, since this SKILL.md's canonical demo fixture is cross-sectional) and add a comment showing random_effects=c('SubjectID') as the pattern for a true repeated-measures fixture, or add a Common Errors row for the exact 'number of levels of each grouping factor' message with the same explanation already given for LinDA.

recommendations.title: Shared WSL lefse env is broken for both LDA and SVM ranking, independently reproduced -- needs a tooling-pass fix, not a SKILL.md change
recommendations.problem: run_lefse.py crashes on any input (confirmed on a fresh, independently-built input file, not reusing the fixer's) with a None return from its internal rpy2/R interop step, in both the default LDA ranking and the -r svm alternative.
recommendations.root_cause: R in the shared lefse env is 4.5.3, not the R 3.2/3.3 TOOLS.md describes rpy2 as needing -- a version mismatch between the 'modern noarch build' of LEfSe 1.1.1 actually installed and the R version it was built to interoperate with via rpy2.
recommendations.fix: A future tooling pass on microbiome-metagenomics-analyst should rebuild the lefse env pinned to an R version rpy2 actually resolves against, then re-verify run_lefse.py end to end before any Skill's LEfSe example is scored as execution-verified.

recommendations.title: Maaslin2() crashes on plot generation with a ggplot2 API-version error when there are real significant results to plot
recommendations.problem: A default Maaslin2() call (plot_heatmap/plot_scatter left at their defaults) that finds real significant associations crashes partway through plotting with '<ggplot2::labels> object is invalid: every label must be named', after already having written all_results.tsv/significant_results.tsv to disk.
recommendations.root_cause: Likely a ggplot2-version mismatch between what Maaslin2 1.20.0's plotting code expects and the env's installed ggplot2 4.0.3 (TOOLS.md records this version); not exercised by the original or this re-audit's other runs because sink()/capture.output() suppressed it or plot_heatmap=FALSE/plot_scatter=FALSE were passed.
recommendations.fix: Either note in SKILL.md's MaAsLin2 section that plot_heatmap=FALSE, plot_scatter=FALSE can be passed to skip plotting entirely (the numeric results are unaffected), or fix the env's ggplot2 pin in a future tooling pass.
